subject: MSA / Order Form — Clarify output ownership, training use, and evidence package
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@heliosai.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on MSA + Order Form — IP & training clarifications

Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — HeliosAI is excited about Redwood's latency and routing controls. Before procurement can move to PO, legal has a couple of discrete asks on the attached order form draft and the MSA redlines:

1) Output ownership: we need confirmation that HeliosAI retains exclusive ownership of customer-generated outputs (including prompts and model-generated content) for productization. Can you point me to the exact MSA language you propose?

2) Training/data use: HeliosAI will not opt-in to any model training. Please confirm Redwood will not use HeliosAI data (prompt/response logs) to continually train or fine-tune foundation models without explicit opt-in.

3) Evidence for procurement: our compliance team needs a short evidence package we can attach to the PO: recent SOC 2 type II report or letter, a data flow diagram showing data residency and retention (we operate in us-east-1), and a short statement on how feedback/telemetry is ingested and stored.

Attached is our procurement team's redline of section Exhibit A (productization rights) where we've added alternate wording — we understand some of this may require legal to triage. Can you confirm timelines? End of quarter is the target.

Thanks,

Sara Lim
Head of Procurement
HeliosAI

Attachment: Helios_OrderForm_Redline_001.docx (document stub)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@heliosai.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA + Order Form — IP & training clarifications

Sara — great to meet you yesterday, thanks for the clear list. Tagging Marissa (legal) and Grace (product/legal ops) so we can get formal language and the evidence packet together. High-level answers now:

- Output ownership: our standard is that customers retain ownership of their data and outputs; for productization rights we distinguish between "customer content" and "service outputs" in the MSA. We can provide proposed redline language that preserves HeliosAI ownership while allowing Redwood to operate and debug the service.

- Training / data use: by default Redwood does not use customer content to update public foundation models. We do have a limited feedback license used for service improvement (non-exclusive, de-identified aggregate telemetry) — but customers can opt-out of that feedback usage. Any use to train shared models would be explicit opt-in and subject to separate terms.

- Evidence: we can assemble a short packet: SOC 2 summary, a data flow diagram showing VPC + region residency, retention policy excerpt, and a telemetry ingestion note. I attached the current order form draft (OrderForm_Draft_v3.pdf) with inline comments.

I'll coordinate with Marissa to draft the specific MSA redline language for Exhibit A and a short legal note for procurement. Proposed timeline: legal redline back to you within 48 business hours; evidence packet by EOD Friday (we'll target 2026-12-24). If HeliosAI needs language faster for procurement we can provide a provisional statement of intent.

Next steps:
- Marissa will draft the MSA redline 
- Provide evidence packet (SOC 2, DFD, retention)
- Share DocuSign-ready order form once language agreed

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attach: OrderForm_Draft_v3.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@heliosai.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@heliosai.com
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA + Order Form — IP & training clarifications

Thanks Karthik — that helps. For speed, procurement asked that we propose an interim clause for Exhibit A that reads: "Customer retains exclusive rights to outputs generated from Customer Content; Redwood may use de-identified aggregate feedback solely for internal service quality improvement and not to train or sell models outside the service."

Would Redwood accept similar provisional wording while legal finalizes the MSA redline? If yes, procurement can proceed with the internal PO approvals and we’ll kick off signature once legal confirms.

Also, please include an explicit statement that logs/telemetry will remain in us-east-1 and be retained 90 days by default (with options to shorten). That is a hard requirement for HeliosAI.

Sara

---
Helios_OrderForm_Redline_001.docx (re-attached)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 14:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA / Order Form — Clarify output ownership, training use, and evidence package

Team — looping you in with a proposed legal play. Draft language below for Exhibit A and a note back to procurement. Please review and comment by EOD tomorrow so we can stick to HeliosAI's timeline.

Proposed Exhibit A snippet (draft):

1) Output Ownership: Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Content and any Outputs derived exclusively from such Customer Content. "Outputs" shall not include Redwood platform improvements which are independently developed and do not incorporate Customer Content.

2) Feedback License: Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use de-identified, aggregated feedback and telemetry for the sole purpose of improving the Redwood service. Redwood shall not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or sell models outside of customer-specific deployments without Customer's prior written consent.

3) Data Residency & Retention: Customer Content will be processed and stored in the customer-specified region (us-east-1). Default retention for request/response logs is 90 days; shorter retention periods can be configured by Customer (see Order Form).

Attachments to provide to Helios procurement (we will redact sensitive items):
- SOC 2 Type II summary (Redwood_Security_Residency_Sheet.pdf)
- Data flow diagram (DFD_customer-data.png)
- Retention policy excerpt (Retention_Policy_2026.txt)

Operational notes: Marcus, can you confirm we can produce the 90-day retention by default for a dedicated customer? Grace, can you prepare the redline version of the MSA and an implementation note for opting out of the feedback license?

If all good I will send Helios a consolidated reply with the provisional clause and a DocuSign readiness ETA.

—Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Security_Residency_Sheet.pdf (pdf stub)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — Clarify output ownership, training use, and evidence package

Sara — thanks for the redline and patience. We can accept the provisional wording Marissa drafted (below) while legal finalizes the MSA. Attached is the evidence packet: SOC 2 summary, a DFD showing us-east-1 residency, and the retention policy excerpt.

Provisional clause (for procurement):

"Customer retains exclusive rights to Outputs generated from Customer Content. Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated feedback solely to improve the Redwood service and will not use Customer Content to train or sell models outside the customer deployment without explicit opt-in."

We will: 
- Send a DocuSign-ready order form by EOD tomorrow with the provisional clause included. (Link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abcdef123456)
- Provide final MSA redline from Marissa within 48 business hours.
- Ensure default log retention is set to 90 days in us-east-1; Marcus will confirm process for enforcement on Dedicated capacity.

Attachments: OrderForm_Draft_v3.pdf, Redwood_Security_Residency_Sheet.pdf, DFD_customer-data.png

If that works, please confirm and procurement can proceed with internal approvals. We'll keep the legal review expedited.

Best,
